/work/vista-digital-banking/.title: Vista Digital Banking
/work/vista-digital-banking/.summary: One shared UI language, adapted for four Vista subsidiaries.

blocks.text: Vista needed a recognisable banking experience across The Gambia, Guinea, Sierra Leone and Burkina Faso. The UI had to work in English and French while accommodating each subsidiary’s currency, regulatory copy and banking requirements. I helped design corporate and retail banking journeys across the four subsidiaries and built a shared design system that allowed local differences. I designed Vista’s debit card and the screens for its loan application flow. My work also covered onboarding, account views, transfers and approvals, alongside campaign graphics and HTML/CSS implementation review.

The banking design shipped across four localised subsidiaries using one shared system. The work brought a consistent Vista interface to English- and French-speaking markets while preserving the local information customers need. ITSS’s Most Outstanding Intern of the Year award names my Vista Bank UI/UX work. The four-subsidiary rollout is delivery scope; post-launch usage and task-completion results were not available to me.

/work/radius-pay4me/.title: Radius / Pay4Me
/work/radius-pay4me/.summary: Designing cross-border payments for the student and the person paying.

blocks.text: Education and immigration payments have deadlines. A parent or relative may be paying for a student in another country, using another currency. I designed sponsored payments, verification, currency visibility, transaction tracking and support. On the website, I organised the information families need before trusting the service enough to install the app.

The design connects the website’s trust-building role to the mobile payment journey. Sponsored payments, verification and transaction status are treated as core parts of that experience. Radius, formerly Pay4Me, reports more than 120,000 registered users, more than 1,500 five-star reviews and average delivery of six hours on business days. These are company-level figures, not results attributed to my design work. Read the published figures .

/work/shortlet-lagos/.title: Shortlet Lagos
/work/shortlet-lagos/.summary: Giving guests and property investors different routes into the same business.

blocks.text: A guest is choosing a place to stay. An investor is deciding what a property share means and what it costs. Combining those decisions would give each audience the wrong information. I designed responsive guest-booking and fractional-investment journeys, supported by research into how guests shortlist properties. The two experiences share a visual system while keeping their decisions separate.

Product and design scope. ₦50,000 is the designed entry threshold, not a return or adoption metric.

blocks.text: Businesses and Web3 teams were finding potential partners across scattered social channels. A shadow scale used as depth hierarchy, so a dropdown, a card and a modal never sit at the same visual altitude.
The colour and effect styles as named tokens - accent, dark and opacity tones on a numeric scale, with elevation as its own set.
The icon set organised into semantic categories - navigation, actions, media, design tools - so an icon is chosen by meaning rather than by scrolling.

/about/.title: About Jamiu Abdulfatai
/about/.summary: Product designer working across fintech, AI products and complex workflows.

blocks.text: I design clear interfaces for payments, banking and complex workflows.
I work across web and mobile, from cross-border payments to banking across four subsidiaries. I’m studying MSc User Experience Design at the University of Brighton.
I’m usually drawn to the part of a product where things get complicated. That’s where I find the most interesting design problems.
I like untangling the things that make digital products difficult to use. Sometimes that means questioning a business rule; sometimes it means finding a simpler way to explain what’s happening.
I enjoy the design process, but I also like understanding how things are built. It helps me make decisions that work beyond the Figma file, and gives me more useful conversations with engineers.

At Brighton, I’m developing my research practice and spending more time questioning the decisions behind interfaces, especially how research and AI can help us design more responsibly. My AI practice is part of that exploration.
When I’m not thinking about interfaces, there’s a good chance I’m somewhere playing football.
Visitors may call or email directly using the portfolio assistant’s contact options. A call starts only if their device initiates it, and an email is an editable draft they choose whether to send.

blocks.text: Product design, model evaluation and working prototypes.

My interest in AI starts with what people actually need to do. At Kremor AI I worked on generated fashion, human review and the operational steps behind production. My evaluation work separately examined model output rather than treating it as user research.
Evaluate the output before designing around it.

At Kremor AI I worked across forensic benchmarking, dataset annotation and qualitative evaluation of LLM and generative-image output, covering complex AI interaction tasks. This was model evaluation alongside product design, not participant usability research.

I use AI to explore options and organise research, then check the source material. I use official guidance to ground early models before testing them with people. I label what is sourced, what is hypothesised and what needs validation.
Risk: what happens when it is wrong?

For Kremor AI, I designed prompt scaffolding, conversational starting points and the connected storefront-to-production workflow. Five operational roles, confirmation gates, permissions and audit history make an open-ended AI experience more controllable.
Chalantwork connects AI-assisted sustainability work to evidence and maker-checker review. Its live platform brings reporting and operational decisions into a governed workflow.
Connect conversation to a real task.
The Bizinc assistant-to-booking concept explores conversational discovery. It remains a proposal until business relevance, live availability and booking impact are validated.
Does the person know what the system did, what still needs their approval and what to do when the answer is wrong?

My technical practice includes LangGraph for graph-based agent flows, Hugging Face for open-source model and agent integration, and React.js for front-end implementation awareness. These support the product design rather than replace it.

I built a personal plugin experiment for careful academic editing: minimal changes, preserved citations and author approval before substantial rewrites. It returns edited text, significant changes and questions to review. It does not promise AI-detector scores.

I built a page-aware portfolio agent that connects a visitor’s question to the current route, conversation context, project knowledge and supporting evidence. That work informs how I structure context for AI-assisted products.

I use Claude, ChatGPT, Codex and Google Antigravity around research synthesis, design exploration, functional prototypes and workflow automation, with human review before output becomes a claim or a shipped experience.
